findings.finding: The plan adds a primary+fallback checkout arm (GitHub mirror first, Gerrit refspec fallback) but never states the failure-disposition contract: what disposition surfaces when the mirror fetch fails, what surfaces when the Gerrit refspec fallback also returns the incident's 502/504, and which leg wins so a transient/retryable failure is not masked by a non-retryable one.
findings.location: Plan — 'Preserve exact-patchset safety by checking out GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION from the GitHub mirror first, falling back to Gerrit refspec only when needed, and verifying any fetched ref resolves to the expected SHA.'
scenarios: Both mirror and Gerrit are transiently unavailable during a fetch: without a stated winner, the fallback's own error could surface as fatal and mask a retryable primary — the same class of masking that motivated this incident.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' note: mirror fetch miss/unreachable is transient -> fall back; Gerrit refspec fetch 502/504 is transient/retryable; when both fail the chain preserves the retryable disposition (retry/exit-11), never surfacing the fallback's failure as fatal; a resolved-SHA mismatch is fatal (permanent).
